sections.title: Entry rules to Sri Lanka
sections.body: Most travelers need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) to visit Sri Lanka, which can be applied for online. Passports should be valid for at least six months beyond your date of entry. Make sure to keep this in mind when planning your travel.
bullets: Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) required for most travelers
Passport must be valid for a minimum of six months after entry
Visa can be obtained online prior to arrival
sections.source: Department of Immigration and Emigration, Sri Lanka

sections.title: What February is like in Sri Lanka
sections.body: February is one of the best months to visit Sri Lanka, with warm temperatures and relatively low rainfall in most parts. Expect daytime temperatures around 28-32°C (82-90°F) and cooler evenings. Pack lightweight clothing and sunscreen.
bullets: Average temperatures range from 28-32°C (82-90°F)
Low rainfall makes it great for outdoor activities
Pack light clothing and sunscreen

sections.title: How to handle money in Sri Lanka
sections.body: In Sri Lanka, cash is still king. Many small shops and street vendors only accept cash, so it’s wise to carry some local currency (Sri Lankan Rupee). ATMs are widely available in cities, and credit cards are accepted at larger establishments.
bullets: Use Sri Lankan Rupees for most transactions
ATMs are common in urban areas
Credit cards accepted in larger hotels and restaurants

sections.title: Airport transfer options in Sri Lanka
sections.body: For getting from Bandaranaike International Airport to Colombo, taxis or rideshare services are reliable options. Expect the journey to take about 30-45 minutes and cost around 3,000-4,500 LKR depending on traffic. Airport buses are available but are less comfortable.
bullets: Taxis cost around 3,000-4,500 LKR to Colombo
Journey takes about 30-45 minutes
Airport buses are an option but less comfortable

sections.title: Navigating cities in Sri Lanka
sections.body: Transportation within cities is quite manageable. Tuk-tuks are a popular choice for short distances, and though ride-hailing apps are available, they may fluctuate in availability. Public buses are cheap but can be overcrowded; plan accordingly.
bullets: Tuk-tuks are widely available for short trips
Ride-hailing apps like PickMe and Uber function in major cities
Public buses are inexpensive but often crowded

sections.title: Eating and drinking in Sri Lanka
sections.body: Sri Lankans generally eat rice and curry for lunch, while dinner can range from lighter meals to more elaborate dishes. Street food is popular; don't miss trying kottu roti and hoppers. Always check the cleanliness of food stalls before eating.
bullets: Lunch usually consists of rice and curry
Street food like kottu roti is a must-try
Check food stall hygiene before eating

sections.title: Cultural norms in Sri Lanka
sections.body: Respect for local customs is important. When visiting temples, dress modestly and remove shoes. It's common to greet with a slight bow and a smile, and public displays of affection are generally frowned upon.
bullets: Dress modestly for temple visits
Always remove shoes before entering temples
Public displays of affection may be frowned upon

sections.title: Health recommendations for Sri Lanka
sections.body: Check with your healthcare provider about vaccinations such as Typhoid and Hepatitis A before traveling. Bring a basic first-aid kit and any personal medications. Mosquito repellent is also advised due to dengue fever risks.
bullets: Vaccinations for Typhoid and Hepatitis A recommended
Bring a first-aid kit and personal medications
Mosquito repellent is useful for avoiding dengue fever

sections.title: Intercity travel tips in Sri Lanka
sections.body: Travel between cities is best done via train for scenic views or by bus for cost-effectiveness. Buses are straightforward, but trains can be crowded during peak hours. Booking train tickets in advance is advisable.
bullets: Train travel offers scenic views
Buses are cheaper and more direct
Book train tickets in advance during peak times

sections.title: SIM cards and connectivity in Sri Lanka
sections.body: Buying a local SIM card at the airport or in shops in Colombo is convenient. Dialog and Mobitel offer good coverage and data plans. Internet access is generally reliable in urban areas.
bullets: Local SIM cards available at the airport
Dialog and Mobitel offer good services
Reliable internet access in cities

sections.title: Electrical plugs and voltages in Sri Lanka
sections.body: Sri Lanka uses type D and G plugs with a standard voltage of 230V. Ensure your devices are compatible or bring an adapter. Most hotels provide adapters, but it's good to check in advance.
bullets: Type D and G plugs used
Standard voltage is 230V
Confirm availability of adapters at hotels
